question: On its opening day in 2000, London's Millennium Bridge swayed so alarmingly it was nicknamed the 'Wobbly Bridge.' What made the wobble feed on itself?
choices: Gusts of wind struck the flat deck at just the wrong rhythm
The steel cables stretched unevenly in the summer heat
Ordinary pedestrians unconsciously fell into step with the sway, amplifying it
Soldiers marching across in lockstep hit the bridge's natural frequency
anchorText: an unconscious tendency to match their footsteps to the sway

question: Not one bridge crosses the main stem of the Amazon, among the mightiest rivers on Earth. Why not?
choices: It runs mostly through roadless rainforest, so there is little need for one
It is simply too wide for any bridge to span
Treaties among the Amazon-basin nations forbid building across it
Its bed is too soft and shifting to anchor bridge piers
anchorText: This is not because the river would be too wide to bridge
